newsitem.title: FRANCE: Fundamentalists kill 28 in Algeria - security forces.
newsitem.headline: Fundamentalists kill 28 in Algeria - security forces.

text.p: Moslem fundamentalists killed 28 people in an attack in the early hours of Sunday in the village of Dhamnia in Ain Defla province, some 120 km (75 miles) southwest of Algiers.
Security forces, in a statement on the official Algerian news agency APS, said the 28 were killed by a "group of terrorists", Algeria's official term for Moslem fundamentalists.

The statement on the attack in the village was issued shortly after security forces reported that a bomb had exploded in an Algiers cafe on Sunday. The official provisional toll in the bombing was put at 20 wounded, but hospital sources and witnesses said 53 people were wounded.
It was the fourth bomb attack in under one week. Earlier bombings were blamed on Moslem fundamentalists.

Sunday's blast in a popular cafe in the main square of the working class El Harrach district brought the reported toll from bombings in the capital to at least 18 dead and 210 wounded in under one week.
The security forces said the bomb went off at around 10.30 a.m. (0930 GMT) in the southern suburb of El Harrach. The bomb was the second such attack on a cafe in the capital Algiers in three days.
